summary.text: Toby Ann Stavisky is the Democratic incumbent for New York State Senate District 11 in Queens and is seeking re-election against Republican and Conservative Party candidate Pamela Michos.
A former high school social studies teacher, she was first elected to the Senate in 1999, chairs the Committee on Higher Education and serves as Vice President Pro Tempore.

paragraphs.text: Stavisky was born in New York City and graduated from the Bronx High School of Science.
She earned a B.A. from Syracuse University, where her Senate biography says she attended on an academic scholarship, and master's degrees from Queens College and Hunter College.
She worked as district manager for Northeast Queens for the 1980 U.S. Census, in the actuarial department of an insurance company, and as a social studies teacher in New York City high schools.
Her husband, Leonard Stavisky, a university professor, chaired the Assembly Education Committee and later served in the State Senate until his death in June 1999.
Toby Ann Stavisky was first elected to the State Senate on November 2, 1999, and has been re-elected thirteen times since, according to her Senate biography.
She was the first woman from Queens County elected to the New York State Senate and the first woman to chair the Senate's Higher Education Committee.
Stavisky serves as Vice President Pro Tempore of the Senate and chairs the Committee on Higher Education.

She also sits on the Education, Ethics and Internal Governance, Finance, Judiciary, Racing, Gaming and Wagering, and Women's Issues committees, and she is a trustee of the City University Construction Fund, a member of the Higher Education Capital Matching Grants Board and treasurer of the Legislative Women's Caucus.
According to her Senate biography, she lives in Whitestone and has one son.
